sources.title: Delta Repair: second-day replication
sources.provenance: Original fictional course dossier, issue #181, v1

passages.quote: Fictional independent experiment V20261125-EV-E-Q2, family V20261125-EV-F-Q, used a second deterministic day with changed leg start times, still 40 legs and 10 trucks with the same finite shared charger counts and EVBench R1 timing procedure. Delta Repair produced a checked feasible plan in 51 seconds. This is a new run, unlike the V20261125-EV-S08 digest and V20261125-EV-S09 slides.

Delta Repair thus has two independent shared-charger experiments in this dossier: V20261125-EV-E-Q1 and V20261125-EV-E-Q2, both below 60 seconds. They share a method family, not an experiment identity. Two tested deterministic days do not establish reliability on arbitrary or uncertain future demand.

sources.title: Correction: Cedar Ledger reference timing
sources.provenance: Original fictional course dossier, issue #181, v1
sources.reporting_relationship: correction to V20261125-EV-S05, not an independent experiment

passages.quote: Correction to V20261125-EV-S05 and experiment V20261125-EV-E-L1 (family V20261125-EV-F-L): the 46-second run accidentally omitted shared charger occupancy constraints. Re-running the full Cedar Ledger formulation with those constraints took 93 seconds under EVBench R1. Replace the 46-second time and the earlier eligible claim: Cedar Ledger models shared capacity but is ineligible under the 60-second limit. Its capacity-modelling description in V20261125-EV-S02 remains valid.

The corrected experiment retains identity V20261125-EV-E-L1. The initial and corrected timings are two reports about this one experiment, not independent support. The correction changes the timing/eligibility conclusion, not Cedar Ledger into the Private formulation.

sources.title: Cedar Ledger: private-depot scheduling
sources.provenance: Original fictional course dossier, issue #181, v1

passages.quote: Cedar Ledger Private (cedar-private) gives every truck its own always-available charger. It checks individual energy and charging power but has no depot occupancy sum. It does not model a finite shared charger pool; calling it Cedar Ledger without the Private suffix confuses two different formulations.

sources.title: Delta Repair: shared-depot scheduling
sources.provenance: Original fictional course dossier, issue #181, v1

passages.quote: Delta Repair (delta-repair) fixes candidate truck routes for a repair pass, then allocates charging against a per-depot, per-type, per-slot occupancy ledger. A slot is usable only while its count is below the finite charger count. Conflicts move to another valid waiting slot or trigger leg cancellation and route rebuilding; an unresolved conflict is never returned as feasible.

Delta Repair assumes the same known deterministic inputs and 30-minute whole-wait, lossless constant-power charging as V20261125-EV-S01:P02. It checks coverage, deadheads and return home, truck and charger power, maintenance, battery bounds and final state of charge after repair or cancellation. Fixed candidate routes and repair-or-cancel make this a feasible-plan heuristic, with no claim of global cost optimality.

sources.title: Dossier scope and common assumptions
sources.provenance: Original fictional course dossier, issue #181, v1

passages.quote: This fictional catalogue contains exactly three candidate methods: Cedar Ledger (cedar-ledger), Delta Repair (delta-repair), and Cedar Ledger Private (cedar-private). Only Cedar Ledger and Delta Repair model limited shared charger capacity. The private edition is a title distractor, not another shared-capacity method.

Both shared-capacity methods assume deterministic, known legs, travel times, energy use, tariffs and charger availability for the whole day. Both use 30-minute slots, require each charge to fit wholly inside a depot wait, and assume lossless charging at constant power bounded by the truck and charger ratings. These are modelling assumptions, not evidence about uncertain demand.

Every fictional timing below uses EVBench R1: one thread on the same illustrative reference CPU, including model construction and search until the first complete feasible daily plan passes coverage, sequence, charging, maintenance and state-of-charge checks. A solve need not prove optimality. The acceptance limit is at most 60 seconds; it is not a forecast for student hardware.

sources.title: Delta Repair: reference timing bulletin
sources.provenance: Original fictional course dossier, issue #181, v1

passages.quote: Fictional experiment V20261125-EV-E-Q1, family V20261125-EV-F-Q, ran Delta Repair on a P01-shaped deterministic 40-leg, 10-truck day using shared finite slow and fast charger pools. Its complete feasible plan passed all EVBench R1 checks in 34 seconds, including charger occupancy. This supports eligibility under the 60-second limit for this tested setting, not optimality or a universal runtime guarantee.

sources.title: Dossier boundary and decision scope
sources.provenance: Original fictional course dossier, issue #181, v1

passages.quote: All methods, authors, experiment results and timings in V20261125-EV-S01 through V20261125-EV-S12 are original fiction for this course, not findings attributed to a real paper. P01 supplies a scheduling problem only. There is no uncertain-demand experiment, numerical cost table or evidence of cost superiority in this A/B dossier.

For the tested shared-charger setting with a 60-second solve limit, recommend Delta Repair conditionally on the stated assumptions. Cedar Ledger can represent the chargers but the corrected full solve is too slow; Cedar Ledger Private is fast but cannot represent their sharing. This is eligibility among the three documented methods, not a claim that Delta Repair is always fastest or cheapest.

sources.title: Cedar Ledger: reference timing bulletin

passages.quote: Initial fictional report V20261125-EV-E-L1, family V20261125-EV-F-L: Cedar Ledger completed in 46 seconds on the 40-leg, 10-truck P01-shaped deterministic day. sources.title: Cedar Ledger: shared-depot scheduling
sources.provenance: Original fictional course dossier, issue #181, v1

passages.quote: Cedar Ledger (cedar-ledger) is a mixed-integer daily-cost model. Binary truck-leg assignments and cancellations, deadhead links and charge-slot choices enforce coverage and the truck day. For each depot, charger type and slot, the sum of simultaneous charging trucks cannot exceed the available charger count. It therefore represents limited shared capacity, including separate slow and fast pools.

Cedar Ledger uses the deterministic 30-minute, whole-wait, lossless constant-power assumptions in V20261125-EV-S01:P02. It enforces truck and charger power bounds, maintenance exclusion, intermediate battery bounds and final home state of charge at least the initial level. It may optimise cost, but a time-limited feasible solution is not an optimality certificate.
